[--disable <name>]... [--enable <name>]... [--manual <name>]... [--] <file>
vehicle_sil_launch run [--json | --events [--events-stall-ms <ms>]] [--stdin-commands] [--start-paused]
[--control <address> [--control-credentials <file>] [--control-tls-cert <file>
--control-tls-key <file>] [--control-audit-log <file>]]
[--scenario <file>] [--speed <speed>] [--strict] [--log-dir <dir>]
[--timeout-ms <ms>]
[--describe-timeout-ms <ms>]
[--disable <name>]... [--enable <name>]... [--manual <name>]... [--] <file>
vehicle_sil_launch version [--json]
check <file>                compare the simulation configuration <file> (YAML or JSON) with what each
ecu_main executable in it reports (--describe); list the participants,
the networks and every error and warning
run <file>                  check <file>; if it passes, run the simulation: the registry and the
controller in this process, each participant as a process of its own
(its output on stderr, each line after [<name>]); then end every
participant and report how each ended. Ctrl+C stops it in order
version                     the version of vehicle_sil_launch (--json: also its formats and features)
--json                      write the result as JSON
--events                    run: write what happens as events on stdout, one JSON object per line, the
result last (nothing on stderr but the launcher's own failures)
--events-stall-ms <ms>      run --events: give up a reader of the events that takes nothing for <ms>, and wait
at most <ms> for it to take the result (1000 or more; default 30000)
--stdin-commands            run: read commands from stdin, one JSON object per line: {"command":"stop"}
stops in order (twice: without waiting); the end of stdin stops as well;
pause, resume, step (with "ms") and speed (with "value") control the time
--start-paused              run --stdin-commands or --control: stand still at 0 until a resume or step
command (with --control: before the first step, so that a client's writes
take effect at 0)
--control <address>         run: serve the Control API (gRPC) for clients: the ECUs' variables and the
time; <port> (on 127.0.0.1; 0: any free port), <host>:<port> or unix:<path>;
the event control_server and a line say where (only in a build with
VEHICLE_SIL_BUILD_CONTROL_SERVER=ON)
--control-credentials <file> run --control: tokens and roles, one per line: <role> <name> <token>
(every call then needs a token; never put a token on the command line)
--control-tls-cert <file>   run --control: PEM certificate chain of the server (with --control-tls-key: TLS)
--control-tls-key <file>    run --control: PEM private key of the server
--control-audit-log <file>  run --control: append who changed what
--scenario <file>           check: also check the scenario <file> against the participants' variables;
run: then run it: write the ECUs' variables and compare their values at
virtual times, stop the simulation when the scenario is over, and fail if a
step failed (docs/scenario.md; not with --control or --start-paused)
--speed <speed>             run: simulation seconds per wall-clock second (1 real time, 2 twice as fast)
or max (as fast as possible); replaces speed in <file>
--strict                    fail on warnings too
--log-dir <dir>             run: also write each participant's output to <dir>/<name>.log
--timeout-ms <ms>           run: abort the simulation if it has not ended <ms> after its start (wall clock;
with --start-paused and --control, from when it stands still before the start)
--describe-timeout-ms <ms>  how long one executable may take for --describe (default 10000)
--disable <name>            leave the participant <name> out (as enabled: false in <file>); repeatable
--enable <name>             take the participant <name> in (as enabled: true in <file>); repeatable
--manual <name>             you start the participant <name> yourself (from a debugger, say): run does not
start it, prints the command to start it with and waits for it to join, with
no time limit (as manual: true in <file>); repeatable
--help, -h                  this text
--version                   as version
--                          what follows is the file, also if it starts with '-'
exit codes: 0 passed, 1 errors (with --strict: or warnings; run: also a failed simulation), 3 the file
cannot be read (run: or the registry cannot be set up), 4 usage, 130 run was interrupted (or stopped)
the file format, the rules, the run and the events: docs/simulation-config.md; scenarios: docs/scenario.md
